book_paragraphs: Welcome to our refreshed institutional underwriting dossier on the State Street Health Care Select Sector SPDR ETF, ticker XLV. Here is our verdict up front. On business quality, XLV earns Compounder Pass with Pass With Watch KPI health. book_subsections.title: Before We Begin Chapter 1
paragraphs: Every figure in this monograph is anchored to primary SEC filings, CMS releases, State Street holdings data, and the verified November 24, 2026 session close. Let us walk through the evidence chapter by chapter.

Keep two guardrails in mind as you read. First, we never compromise on cash discipline in a 10-distribution-day Downtrend when portfolio cash sits at 8.73% vs. a 22.0% floor. Second, we let our ratcheted $164.30 stop and $176.46–$180.95 pullback shelf govern every entry with zero FOMO.
Let us begin Chapter 1 by stripping away the ticker price and examining XLV's 1998 Select Sector SPDR architecture from the ground up.

book_subsections.title: What Changed Since Our November 20 Dossier
paragraphs: A refresh is only valuable when it challenges the prior report rather than rubber-stamping it. Between November 20 and November 24, 2026, three major developments reshaped the evidence base. First, CMS finalized IPAY 2028 negotiated Medicare prices on November 23 for 13 drugs instead of the 15 initially selected—bringing the cumulative IRA cohort to 37 drugs—while excluding AbbVie’s Botox under court order and removing Pfizer’s Xeljanz on generic entry. Second, the FDA approved AbbVie’s RINVOQ as the first systemic therapy for nonsegmental vitiligo, helping lift XLV 2.95% on November 24 to $184.72 even as the S&P 500 slipped 0.49%.

Third, our price-blind Pass 1 audit surfaced three genuine blind spots that the earlier monograph had under-analyzed: $100.0 billion in CY2025 federal 340B hospital drug discounts (+23% year-over-year), external clinical competition from Akeso and Summit Therapeutics’ ivonescimab showing a 27% mortality reduction versus Merck’s Keytruda, and constituent balance-sheet overhangs at AbbVie ($80.8 billion in debt and -$5.94 billion negative equity) and Johnson & Johnson (~$5.5 billion Q3 ovarian talc charge). Incorporating all three keeps XLV at Compounder Pass quality with Pass With Watch KPI health while reinforcing our disciplined WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT posture.
